raj: quick design call: saved per-route views that include a model filter 1 should we persist routing as hard (region/tier inline) or soft (resolve on open/apply)? pros/cons? cc @tara @leo

tara: short: soft by default. infra changes a lot, hard-pinning will surprise users and break rollouts. but we need a clear snapshot so people can reproduce numbers.

leo: can we have both? store a small "snapshot" + a "live_resolution" policy. UI shows snapshot by default with a toggle -> "live". snapshot = resolved routing + perf/cost estimate at save time.

anya: telemetry/metrics angle: if we only store snapshot we still want to know what actually ran. must emit resolved_routing, model_rev, effective_sample_rate on apply. otherwise QA can't correlate regressions.

raj: what if snapshot is computed only at save-time and we store it as a blob:
```json
{"snapshot_routing":"us-west-2/dedicated-medium","snapshot_cost_estimate_tokens":1200,"snapshot_latency_ms":145}
```
and then we also keep a policy field: "resolution": "soft" | "hard" | "prefer_snapshot".

tara: that seems OK. prefer_snapshot is interesting for users who want "mostly live but prefer my saved environment".

leo: UX: show a banner when snapshot differs from live resolution: "Saved snapshot: us-west-2/dedicated-medium. Current resolve: eu-west-1/burst. Use snapshot / Use live". default to snapshot for reproducibility, but warn about cost/latency implications.

anya: telemetry events we should add:
- saved_view_saved (include snapshot fields if present)
- saved_view_previewed (include live_resolve vs snapshot_diff boolean)
- saved_view_applied (resolved_routing_id, model_rev, sample_rate, route_id, user_id)
This will let us build audits and drift dashboards.

raj: quota interplay: if a saved view prefers snapshot that points to dedicated capacity the apply-step may be throttled or rejected. we need a graceful fallback: policy order = [try snapshot, fallback to route-defaults, fallback to cheapest-compatible]. show rejection reason in UI with action buttons.

leo: implementation sketch for API v3 payload (stringified in saved object):
```json
{
  "v": "v3",
  "route": "r_42",
  "model_filter": "open-13b@rev-2025-07",
  "filters": [{"field":"status","op":":","value":"error"}],
  "snapshot": "{...}",
  "resolution_policy": "prefer_snapshot",
  "sampling_hint": "0.1"
}
```
(note: actual saved object stores snapshot as a small string blob to keep the DB schema stable)

anya: small note: sampling_hint should be explicit and we should use a float 0..1. analytics ETA depends on it. also track sampling_owner = route|view|global.

ops-bot: cluster-check: dedicated pools referenced in snapshot must be discoverable by resolver service. If not found, resolver returns FALLBACK_NOT_FOUND.

raj: migration plan: read v1 objects, compute snapshot using resolver, and write v3 with resolution_policy=soft and snapshot filled. do background backfill at low QPS. expose both formats in read API for a month before forcing v3.

tara: rollout: gate preview that makes live resolve calls behind a feature flag. we should A/B 10% first to measure latency impact and error surface.

leo: I'll draft the UI mock that includes snapshot/live toggle + rejection states. will post a link in this thread.

anya: I'll add telemetry schemas to the analytics repo and wire up example dashboards to detect drift and failed reapplies.

raj: ok owners: leo -> UI mock + copy, anya -> telemetry events + dashboards, tara -> rollout plan + feature flag, raj -> API + migration RFC.

ops-bot: workflow: saved-view-migration-job queued @2198880055 (job/8921).

leo: thanks all, will follow up with mocks.

raj: great, capturing in ticket INF-2043. closing thread here. :)
